entry.title: 20/11/26 Barnsley 1-2 SWFC: Not so easy does it as Owls go third

link.title: 20/11/26 Barnsley 1-2 SWFC: Not so easy does it as Owls go third

entry.content:
Introduction

In a thrilling local derby, Sheffield Wednesday secured a 2-1 win away at Barnsley. The match was full of surprises, with Jamal Lowe’s brace and some questionable defensive plays. Let’s dive into the highlights and what it means for the team’s future.

20/11/26 Barnsley 1-2 SWFC: Not so easy does it as Owls go third

Five Minute View From The Kop

You've got a side that's fighting at the bottom of the table who were just passing the ball around us and getting it forward, but I mean, ultimately, I think even their goal that they scored to make it to one was just a matter of him being there in the right time and it hit him and went in.

Episode transcript

Wednesday five-minute view from The Kop after a 2-1 win away at Barnsley. Now, Barnsley, 23rd in the table, we knew they would put up a fight, especially with it being a local derby. There was always a bit of niggle between Wednesday and Barnsley, and we put out pretty much an unchanged team, which was good, and we had more options on the bench. So, we did wonder whether Keyla Dunn would be the one scoring a goal against his old team.

A lot of the Barnsley fans beforehand said it was nailed on. They were expecting to lose. Now, they did lose, but the manner in the game was quite interesting. It’s always going to be difficult. Local derby fans aren’t going to win there. They’re always going to step up. You do wonder why. So, Wednesday play against the team and they can make anybody look like Barcelona on the day. You’ve got a side that’s fighting at the bottom of the table who were just passing the ball around us and getting it forward, but I mean, ultimately, I think even their goal that they scored to make it to one was just a matter of him being there in the right time and it hit him and went in.

Jamal Lowe’s Double Stuns the Opponent

But Jamal Lowe early doors was star of the show, scoring a brace which is pretty amazing. So, he scored in the eighth minute and the 14th minute, and at that point, we looked very comfortable. When the first goal went in, it just seemed to knock them, and then they came back into a little bit. We scored again, and we just thought, well, I mean, will that shut them up, you know, we can just push on from there.

Defensive Nerves and Scrappy Play

But yeah, they controlled most of the first half after that point, and interestingly, through the whole match, we only had two shots on target. So, two shots, two shots on target, which is okay. I mean, the challenger will say it’s the result that matters. That’s the important thing. But for me, after that sort of 14th minute, really, you look at the match, and we did have our opportunities. We had some big chances throughout, but we spent a lot of the time on the back foot.

It was quite scrappy, and we were giving the ball away quite a lot. I thought Bannon had a decent game. I think they ended up fetching him off just to protect him really. I mean, that’s the way. But Bannon and Mitchell both ended up coming off, and I have no idea what happened to the midfield after that point. But they were just launching the ball in, and they didn’t really look. Yeah, I think we just sort of handled them quite well.

Blumley was having a good game. Cooper very good in the middle. Bernard, yeah, another assured performance. I mean, other than that, yeah, slightly we’re getting stuck in, but Mitchell got a yellow card. Keyla Dunn were just absolutely feeding off scraps, so really, he didn’t really get much of an opportunity. He did get an opportunity at one point which looked like a certain goal, but the defender just came across as he’d headed the ball towards a space on the goal and actually cleared it.

So, a bit disappointing for him really. He would have liked to have probably got one over on them. But Wednesday won, and we are third in the table, so that’s good, but I think you know, challenge has got to have a lot to say to these players afterwards. We knew it’d be a scrap, but I think we just make things much harder than really they need to be. And I wouldn’t like to hope that if this is gonna be one of the worst teams in the division that we’re playing against that we are not gonna have an easy time.

I mean, we had an easy time of the Plymouth game. I think as has been said by some, I think sometimes we just slip back into what we’ve always done. When we were going forward right at the beginning of their match and in a few little spells, we look great. We look really good, but at times, we just look like we can never find one of our own players. So, yeah, fortunately, we had that speller right at the start.

So, other than the standard starting lineup, we ended up having to make our five subs, you know, and I’ve made a big thing about the five subs, but we got Palmer in for Sil Swinkels, Leongola in for Jamal Law, Louie Barry in for Barry Mitchell, Barry Swap, Harry Gray for Barry Bannon, and Ricardo Santos for Di’Shon Bernard.

Substitutions and Player Adjustments

Yeah, in the end, I can’t say it was comfortable at all, but it’s 2-1. We’re third in the league, we’re just going to push on from here, hopefully, with the players coming back with more training time with Charlie Net, we’re gonna be able to adapt more to the way that we want to play. Another thing as well about looking at the average positions, the players I thought we were quite narrow. I think that when Gray came on, he stretched it a bit, Santos played a bit further back, and Gray played a bit further forward, so we were stretching a little bit, but certainly before the substitutions, we were very narrow as in not necessarily we were using the width of the pitch, but there were players that were mostly hardly getting over the halfway line, so that’s not good.

I’m sure Dave will sort it out. Okay, that’s it from me until next time. See you later, we’re all Wednesday, aren’t we?

entry.summary: Sheffield Wednesday made very hard work of a game against almost bottom of the table. Barnsley two early goals and then they clung on and ran out two one winners

entry.title: 14/11/26 SWFC 3-0 Plymouth: Here we go. Goals and hot water

link.title: 14/11/26 SWFC 3-0 Plymouth: Here we go. Goals and hot water

entry.content:
Introduction

Sheffield Wednesday delivered a convincing 3-0 victory over Plymouth at home, with Billy Mitchell’s goal breaking the deadlock and a spirited second-half showing. Dave Challinor’s debut as manager was a success, and there was a special moment when hot water was available on The Kop for the first time in memory. Let’s dive into the highlights of the game.

14/11/26 SWFC 3-0 Plymouth: Here we go. Goals and hot water

Five Minute View From The Kop

And just another note as well, that we had hot water for the first time in, I don't know whether we've ever had hot water on the, on The Kop, but actually went in to the toilets. It's quite a big deal.

Episode transcript

Sheffield Wednesday, five-minute view from The Kop, absolutely fantastic day. Wednesday beating Plymouth, 3-0 at home. Putting out a side to start off with that actually looked like a side that could compete. Lumley back, Bernard fit enough, Cooper back, Swinkels back, Billy Mitchell back. So, and then on the bench we’d got, we got Gray and Barry as well. So that were, you know, that were a good start. But I think, I thought first off we we actually rode our luck a little bit in that sense. That actually they add, they seem to be the more dangerous team, they seem to have more opportunities. A bit of a combination of a little bit of slight defending, good goalkeeping, good to see Lumley back that he played really well. And actually, you know, after sustained pressure and it looked like they were going to be the ones that were, they were growing more into the, into the game. We actually nicked a goal just before half-time.

Billy Mitchell breaks the deadlock

A great goal, Billy Mitchell, absolutely welted it, took a massive deflection. But it was going in anyway, it’s attributed to him. And then coming out second half, and you did wonder because as has been mentioned to me, in quite a lot of times we come out second half and it’s as if we’ve just sort of been relaxing a little bit and we’ve not, we’ve not really had some home truths. And I think there were some home truths after that first half, even though we went in at one nil, the fact is that they were getting the better of us at times. So it was interesting to see what had actually happened after that point.

The second-half battle and goals

We actually came out second half and I thought we battled for everything. We were physical and quite often I’ve said that we’re just not physically enough. We were, it was scrappy at times, but we were actually getting stuck in and we were putting bodies on the line. We were going in for some tough challenges. They were trying to get penalties and free kicks all the time. But yeah, I mean, we, we managed to get through that and as time went on, it really looked like it was going to be us that were going to be the ones getting the goals. And actually you did wonder whether it was going to get to a stage where we had going to last sort of like 10 minutes and we’d be fighting to try and keep it as a win and not leveling up. So, I mean, the thing is we were wondering at what point, at what point you’re going to, you’re going to fetch Louis Barry on, at what point you’re going to fetch Harry Gray on. We’d got Jamel Lowe that was sort of out on that left side, but they did keep him on, at least at first. And we popped up with Davis Keillor-Dunn, who actually does excel in that centre role. You know, he was sort of playing the centre forward and really could be the answer, really could be the answer for us. He’s the one that’s going to be playing the centre forward. We just need to make sure that he’s not going back in January, keep him if we can. And then pretty much straight after that, Di’Shon Bernard, who I thought has been pushing up quite a little bit recently and I did have a little bit of a dig at him because I thought that we conceded a goal in one of the previous matches because he’d already committed himself forward, but came forward and he sort of got to a situation where he could only really shoot, he weren’t going anywhere, there weren’t really anybody for him to pass to, and he absolutely rifled it in. Thought at first the goalkeeper had saved it, but actually he just parried it and it went in right in the corner. So, yeah, so he, you know, 3-0 at 82 minutes and it just ended up being a little bit of a canter at the end, it was just so easy. And I, you know, you can’t put it down to the quality of the opposition. I mean, this is a team that have been doing a better away than they have at home. Yes, I know beforehand I was talking about the fact that it was the lower teams that they were playing, but you know, this is a team that’s going to be up there. They did look quite fairly handy in the first, in the first half, but I think, you know, again, you look at our, our team and, you know, we should, we should be competing. And I think, you know, Dave Challinor would be pleased that he’s got the right reaction and actually we’re not just started with a win at home, first match proper under his tenure, first league match proper under his tenure, but actually a very, very convincing win and a well-deserved win in the end. You know, it was really only us that were pushing for it. We did ride his luck, but you know, the important thing is how many times are we not taking the chances and we’ve ended up getting sucker punched happens so often. So we, we did that this time and just showed that we’ve got, we have got enough players when, when they fit, we’ve got enough players to, to be competitive in this, in this league. So absolutely fantastic today.

Hot water on The Kop for the first time

And just another note as well, that we had hot water for the first time in, I don’t know whether we’ve ever had hot water on the, on The Kop, but actually went in to the toilets. It’s quite a big deal. The taps generally just add blue, blue dots on them, red dots, and it was at least warm that was coming out. So fantastic. So let’s, let’s hope that we keep this going and let’s hope for another good week of players coming back from injury and that we’ve not got any new ones coming out of this one, but fantastic. Absolutely brilliant. And yes, we’re all Wednesday, don’t we? Bye for now.

Expect some candid commentary from the Kop as we analyze the team’s readiness for the upcoming league games.

11/11/26 SWFC 0-4 Accrington: Lambs to the slaughter

Five Minute View From The Kop

George Brown showed some strength, uh Akpobi did did well in a couple of spells to show that he could he's got a turn and he can take people on.

Episode transcript

Chiffier Wednesday, five-minute view from The Kop after a quite humiliating 4-0 home defeat to League Two, Accrington Stanley, who were there. A bit of a dead rubber match in the Jersey Mike’s trophy, the American sandwich trophy. Yeah, a bit of a dead rubber really, in the sense that we’d already qualified, but we were top and winning the match would have meant that we would have gone to the last 32 with a home match. Losing tonight meant that we were still qualifying but we’d be going to the last 32 with a guaranteed away game against somebody who won their league, so we’ve got a tougher game out of it.

Now we didn’t really know what kind of team Dave Challinor would put out in response to the performance the other day, and the fact that we know that we’ve got a team that are a little bit depleted with injuries. Players coming back gives an opportunity though to get some players having a little bit of time. Didn’t expect that George Brown would be on the bench for the last match, but he actually started up front, got the opportunity to get some time under his belt.

Colonel Truman in goal because we didn’t really have any other opportunity to have that, but we started off with the 3-4-3 and it was Weaver in the middle and Otigbayo and Colm McGee, so I mean that could have almost been the defense from last season when Ernie Weaver would fit.

Billy Mitchell breaks the deadlock

And then a few names that I’m not necessarily familiar with, some I’m familiar with from very very fleeting glimpses before, but so we’ve got Paul and Thornton, Oliver and Fazir in midfield, Akpobe, George Brown and Duro up front so to speak. So they were talking about Otigbayo and Faziri being the two senior players, so the more senior players in the team which is really strange, and actually the average age of our team tonight is 20 years old and that’s with Colonel Truman in the net at 31, so very very inexperienced team.

And you’ve got to set yourself, I mean the bench was not not much better really, we’ve got players like James Kay who’d been out for a while and we did actually utilize all our substitutes, De Oliveira, Liddell, Hatfield, Ano and Kay all sort of came on. entry.title: 08/11/26 Oldham 2-1 SWFC aet: Same old owls

link.title: 08/11/26 Oldham 2-1 SWFC aet: Same old owls

entry.content:
Introduction

Sheffield Wednesday’s FA Cup exit against Oldham has raised plenty of questions about the team’s performance and the new manager’s strategy. Join us as we break down the match and discuss the future of the club under Chaliner’s leadership.

08/11/26 Oldham 2-1 SWFC aet: Same old owls

Five Minute View From The Kop

But yes, it ended up being something else. It started off as a 3-4-3.

Episode transcript

Chiffre Wednesday, five minute view from The Kop, Wednesday going down 2-1 after extra time against Oldham in the FA Cup. A lot of hope, a lot of promise, a lot of talk about new manager, new tactics, whether it had all come a little bit too early. Has he had chance to get to see the team yet? Who’s he going to play? What formation is he going to play? Is it going to be a 3-5-2, is it going to be a 3-4-2-1, which I think we played the last game with, or something else?

And yes, it ended up being something else. It started off as a 3-4-3. Quite interesting that Di’Shon Bernard came back into the side, having said that he has scored a few goals this season, and Palmer came in. Gray was on the bench but apparently got injured on his way to the ground, or something like that, so George Brown I think took his place, but I don’t know whether he was probably not ready, they ended up not using him anyway.

We’ve pretty much dominated the match from a point of view of possession, but I think they probably ended up with more shots than we did, and certainly on target.

Defensive frailties expose weaknesses

For their two goals, again, defensive frailties showing. We lost the goalkeeper Maynard Brewer from coming out, got injured, clashed straight into one of their players, so he went off, and Truman our number three, so we’ve now lost our first two goalkeepers. Truman number three, he came on and I think he did okay, but apart from I think he’s going to take a little bit of responsibility around, when we conceded, he was flapping a little bit as well.

Distribution again at times poor, so yeah, so we ended up going out. They didn’t really seem to trouble us, but yet again we didn’t really trouble them.

Billy Mitchell breaks the deadlock

So we had a lot of possession, Slattery saw a lot of the ball, Keiller-Dunn saw a lot of the ball and actually took his goal well, he scored for us. And yeah, I think, you know, Palmer being in the side, he actually got involved quite a lot, he does get involved, but you know, it’s the quality of what you get out of him. I thought that when Max Lowe came on, we seemed to have more going forward on that side.

We did change things around quite a bit, we weren’t really getting anywhere, and we seemed to seem to push on a little bit more, but again just completely blunt. Di’Malo pretty much did nothing, nothing in that match at all. So we ended up bringing Granger on, and yeah, didn’t really get an opportunity, not many touches at all.

Manager Chaliner’s tactical adjustments

But then again, Di’Malo didn’t really get that many touches when he was on the pitch. And some would say, you know, if that was Harry Kane, he’d be coming back, trying to get hold of the ball. I thought Bannon probably got involved in patches, but not necessarily. Heskey, again, played well in the last match, and I thought he did okay, for the most part. I think, as I said, Bernard, he had quite a good game, he got involved in quite a lot, but I think, you know, for their second goal, I just didn’t see him at all.

Anyway, no idea where he was. But Santos was in defence with him, and again, Santos is quite a slow player, it seemed okay for me, but, you know, whether it’s calm or not, I think Chaliner would be absolutely going ballistic at the players. I think, because they just really, I heard him shouting, faster, you know, and I think we’d been practising, just trying to move that ball quicker. But yeah, we just, whenever we tried to, we were just losing it.

I thought they defended really well, actually, and they probably deserved, they actually deserved to win. So I think, all in all, you know, good luck to them, going forward. What now for us? Well, I think Bernard was struggling at the end, so, you know, I think we might be struggling again with him. And like I say, he’s a quality player, yeah, I mean, we seem to be struggling to get a decent team together, so, you know, let’s see what comes out of this.

Let’s see what Chaliner has to say about it. Let’s see whether we see a similar kind of side against Alteringham, I think, is our next game, um, it’s Alteringham, yeah, so let’s see what happens in the next cup game, whether we see more kids come out, or whether we do see a few players juggle around, yeah, one mentioned Jody Leongola, he also was on, but he was on the left, and you could see, it didn’t really suit him, right-footed player, and he just kept putting it back onto his right foot, whenever they pushed onto him, he always came inside, yeah, and it’s just a little bit too obvious, other than that, I thought he sort of did okay, really, but it would have been nice to have seen him on the left, but, you know, we sort of gave that exclusively to Sil Swinkels, and I don’t know, we’ve got to do something, I’ve got to do something different, um, but that’s, that’s for, uh, challenge to, to work out, and, uh, and see where we get, can’t really knock him for his first game, it’s only been a couple of days, but I think, you know, Wednesday have shown exactly why we’re in the situation that we’re in, good team on paper, it’s just not really working, is it?

Okay, till the next game, uh, bye for now, and, uh, we’re all Wednesday, aren’t we?

entry.title: 01/11/26 SWFC 1-1 Blackpool: Handball!
entry.content:
Introduction

After a mixed performance, Sheffield Wednesday drew 1-1 with Blackpool at Hillsborough. Manager Dave Challinor made his debut, and despite some tactical changes, the team struggled to break through. Billy Mitchell’s goal provided a spark, but the game was far from convincing. Let’s dive into the key moments and analysis of the match.

01/11/26 SWFC 1-1 Blackpool: Handball!

Five Minute View From The Kop

It was right at the other end of the pitch, but it looked to me like a really, really poor tackle. Foot was high, no idea what he was doing but he seemed to have got past but that was Sil Swinkels, got sent off down to 10 men.

Episode transcript

Sheffield Wednesday five minute view from The Kop after the sides finish level at Hillsborough. Sheffield Wednesday one, Blackpool one. Now Blackpool started off down the other end of the table and they have not been doing very well recently. They’ve been struggling with injuries. We’ve sort of covered all this before in the preview. They come into Hillsborough, you know, they just wonder which Wednesday is going to turn up. Is it going to be the Wednesday that struggled against the other sides down at the bottom?

A bit of a mixed bag today and you know, I’m a bit disappointed. Yeah, it’s quite often that you come away from Hillsborough a bit disappointed. Obviously, we’re on a new dawn.

Managerial Implications

They’ve announced that Dave Challinor is going to be a Wednesday manager and I’m looking forward to seeing how things change with him. He apparently was going to be at the game today. They decided not to have him come out. Certainly, I didn’t see right at the beginning of the game but he didn’t come out with anyone at the end. Wednesday, interesting when they announced the team, it looked like they were going to be playing five at the back and I thought, come on, anybody who’s at the wrong end of the table comes to Hillsborough and we go, well, you know, we’re going to play one up front.

We’re going to pack defence and, you know, and then you can come at us. But actually, and interestingly, because I think Challinor quite often prefers a 3-5-2, so it seemed like we went with something like that at the start but it was just the personnel that were a bit strange because we got Palmer in. Out went Reece James, out went Billy Mitchell. We got Palmer and Max Lowe, Sil Swinkels came in and Ernie Weaver, it was good to see him playing in because I thought he had a really good game the other day.

So yeah, it was interesting to see how they sort of played but they did play with a back three, five in midfield and then just hard to really see what were happening up front but he was switching around quite a bit. I think it was probably more like a 3-4-2-1 in that sense with the two being Swinkels and Slattery and Keilah Dunn with bursts out front and actually we let him come on to us a few times.

I mean, you know, people probably just getting used to playing in a little bit of a different formation. I know we did it against Doncaster but, you know, it did sort of concern me. We got on the bench, we got Otugbayo was on the bench but Santos was on and also Jodie Leongola was on.

Billy Mitchell breaks the deadlock

So I suppose it just depended how the game went and after the initial sort of confusion we seemed to grow into the game and we had a long spell of being pretty dominant and when we scored it was a great goal with Keilah Dunn nipping it, nicking it and running on and slotting it right into the corner. Really good to see a player that can actually do that and I thought Keilah Dunn had a really good game actually.

I thought that he seemed to have a little bit more space and maybe, you know, maybe this is the formation that they need to play in but on the wings you’ve got Jan Valery on one side and you’ve got Max Lowe on the other which was probably not how I would have expected it really when you got Gray and Morrison on the bench. So well there we go but anyway so it seemed it seemed to sort of work however we probably laboured a little bit too much against a side that have not really been doing very well.

Some people would say Wednesday on a side that have not been doing very well but there you go and then yeah the sending off looked to me, it was right at the other end of the pitch, but it looked to me like a really, really poor tackle. Foot was high, no idea what he was doing but he seemed to have got past but that was Sil Swinkels, got sent off down to 10 men. Now when one of your three gets sent off you know what, what do you then do and I think we went back to a back four but we sort of kept this side as it was and actually didn’t make any changes at half time either which was quite surprising really.

I think that we did, you know, we did okay. I think we battled to keep things going and, you know, just seemed to be dealing quite well with it and then obviously over time you’ve got less players running around a little bit more so they decided to bring Santos on and I get that and so Santos comes on and pretty much immediately they’d already made loads of subs and at one point I think they brought four on.

Jerry Yates, typical isn’t it, so he’s played for Wednesday, nicked the ball in underneath Maynard Brewer. I don’t know who was at fault at the start, I don’t know who perhaps was the issue at the start, who’d not picked him up running through. Like I say, Santos has only just come on and he slotted into the middle of the defence and Yates managed to nick the ball under Maynard Brewer into the net 1-1 and you’re thinking well where are we going to go from here because I thought we’d not only cope quite well with having less players but we were pushing forward occasionally and actually missed a few relatively half chances I suppose you could say.

So I think eventually we clung on and it ended up being one all, they hit the bar at one point, sort of long shot, I think we’d have probably got it covered in any case but they weren’t that good a side really and so it’s disappointing to really come away with just a draw. Formation wise that one’s quite interesting but I think perhaps with different players I wouldn’t really have expected that we’d have had the back three as we did.

Certainly with other players, other options, but we wanted to risk Santos from the start and like I say Ernie Weaver again, I thought Ernie Weaver played well. I think probably the man of match for me could have been Keilah Dunn, certainly with his goal. I thought Birstow, I know he’s dipped a bit in the ratings but I thought he actually ran quite well today. I thought that Slattery and Keilah Dunn were particularly good in their roles.

Bannon started off quite poorly, he was giving the ball away quite a lot and I thought well this is it, you know the new boss is watching you now but yeah I think he grew into it and did a few typical Bannon things, nicking the ball, bit of a bad tempered game, just one sort of final point on that, so a bit of a bad tempered game. I think that the sending off were justified but it took a long time for them to get a card and it seemed like they could just do whatever they liked.

They were on balls, there were players being brought down and they just let them let them off with it. The one point where the one of their players pushed, I think pushed Max Lowe a couple of times and just got away with it and then there was a bit of an issue with Bannon who’d been niggling a little bit in a couple of tackles with one of their players and he ended up booking both but their player were just pushing Bannon all over the place and yeah I mean a lot of people would have said what’s happening there, although I think their manager also got a card as well out of that because he was saying a few things on the side but it just seemed like they could get away with what they like and I think right at the end of the game I said well one thing to come out of that is the referee’s weekend in Blackpool’s still secure so yeah I think it was not really that good in that sense that I thought the referee had a very poor game but all in all one all I suppose is a result that given that we played for so long with 10 men we will have to just put up with that and it’s a new dawn you know it’s been announced this morning that Challinor has taken over, he’s got a fantastic record will be interesting to see after this who he’s bringing in because he’s got a couple of people that work with him quite regularly so I think he’ll probably end up bringing more in whether I’m sure manages to stay on in some kind of form I don’t know but it’s going to be very very interesting and quite exciting going forward really really looking forward to seeing what the team looks like after is a little bit time to work with them so that I think the next game’s on the 8th against Oxford is it in the in the cup I think not sure um okay well I want to head off thanks for listening if you if you do like these short summaries please like subscribe share it just uh gives me a little bit of no a lot of people listen to this um there’s just not that many people subscribing obviously if you do you get notified when I do more and you know the more people that want to listen and want to watch when I do the Friday um reviews the uh the more it encourages me to uh to make these videos and you know we as I keep saying we’re all Wednesday there’s lots and lots of uh people out there doing pods uh so I just try and make it a little bit different a little bit of a different slant on on things so he’s looking forward to what’s coming up next uh we can put the uh Pederson era to bed and you know good luck to him but you know onwards and upwards for us okay till then bye for now and uh yes again we’re all Wednesday aren’t we

entry.title: 27/10/26 SWFC 1-1 Cambridge: Baby steps forward
entry.content:
Introduction

Welcome back to Sheffield Wednesday’s Five Minute View from The Kop, as they secured a 1-1 draw with Cambridge United, despite the initial struggles. We’ll dive into the game, highlight Billy Mitchell’s goal, and discuss the unexpected moments on The Kop. Stay tuned!

27/10/26 SWFC 1-1 Cambridge: Baby steps forward

Five Minute View From The Kop

I thought that Weaver played excellent in defence, really, really well, got involved in a lot of blocks, a lot of last ditch defending.

Episode transcript

Sheffield Wednesday five-minute view from The Kop, Sheffield Wednesday one, Cambridge United one, at Hillsborough, first match post-Henrik Pedersen, and wondered really what to expect. Wondered really whether we’d change formation, whether we’d change any of the players, and it ended up being the same formation but actually enforced changes. So Cooper was unavailable, so Max Lowe moved across into the middle, partnered by Ernie Weaver with Rhys James on the left hand side, Jan Valle on the right, Bannon and Mitchell in the middle, and then on the left we’d got Keilah Dunn and on the right we’d got Harry Gray.

It was interesting the way that they played those two, Slattery sort of in the middle and then Nathan Birstow up top. So didn’t really know what to expect from this match, didn’t expect that really they’d been able to change anything as such, like I say, you know, we’ve got changes enforced upon us which was going to make us play a little bit different. They came at us, and right at the beginning, we just didn’t seem to be able to put anything together at all.

Passers were just going astray all over the place, same old, same old really. I think you know we’ve seen a lot of that this season. They had a few good chances, I suppose, four big chances I think right at the start, but we weathered these sort of early issues and then we sort of seemed to come into it, and then it became a bit of a competition, and then we seemed to sort of get the edge with the game as it sort of went on.

Billy Mitchell breaks the deadlock

I thought that Weaver played excellent in defence, really, really well, got involved in a lot of blocks, a lot of last ditch defending. Nice to see Reece James back on the left, I think he just gives us more going forward. I think you know and to have him and Max Lowe in there as well is a good thing really, it’s a good option to have. So the side was okay really, I mean, other than Keilah Dunn likes to play centrally, so he’s going to pull in, Gray likes to play on the opposite flank, so he’s going to pull in, and so there were times when they picked the ball up, but really not very wide, we’re not really sort of utilising the width, I mean, it’s a big pitch at Hillsborough, I was thinking that you know we’ve got this massive great big pitch and we should always really be playing with wingers hugging that touchline.

The surprise of hot water on The Kop

It was interesting because Morrison was on the bench and so there was actually the opportunity to play Gray on the left and Morrison on the right, and then maybe I would have probably liked to have seen Keilah Dunn, Slattery up there, but anyway, the way things went, and we pushed more and more and more, and we seem to be dominating possession, we certainly dominate possession, and I think in the first half, they only had about 70 passes, accurate passes, so you know, once we’d weathered those early chances that they had, then it was a matter of time was whether we could actually score a goal, and actually, when it came, it wasn’t against a replay at all, I think you know we thoroughly deserved it, it was a cracking shot by Birstow, and actually just after half time, and I’d said at half time that I didn’t think he’d really done that much in the first half, and obviously, that was a kick up the backside that he needed, came alive, got the ball, welled it, and it smashed against the inside of the post and went into the opposite side of the goal right in front of us, so it was really really good goal, and we seem to push on from there, you know, they they met a few subs, they brought a load of players on to try and turn the game, and I thought we we were still looking the more likely when we went forward, but as usual is the case, well, we had a fantastic chance where we cracked the ball straight at the goal and point blank, the goalkeeper managed to get a really strong arm to it and and kept it over, and from that point, the ball came out, I think it was just after that ball came out, we lost it, didn’t manage to get back, and they just ran all the way up forward, sent it central, I think to to one of their players that they brought on, their number 11, who then smashed it straight into into the net, and it just looks so so simple, and they’ve not really threatened that much, I think, since since the early early times, but you know, that’s Wednesday isn’t it, it’s you know, don’t take advantage of your chances and then get to get punished for it, so I think you know, really, I mean, that was their their goals against from a play, I thought that we were very good value for that one nil, then you just thinking, you know, what’s gonna happen, here we’re gonna end up getting another one or are they gonna and it were a bit backwards and forwards at the end, got quite nervous at one point, we were making some quite bad mistakes, Palmer came on for Jan Vallely and he wellied a ball at one point, and it just went straight to them, and they just came straight back at us, so it was it was a little bit last gasp defending, they look like the more likely to score probably towards the end, I mean, we had our opportunities as well, we brought our comedy on, and Swinkels came on, which is good to see, so it gives us another option at the back, we even went off and thought he might have been injured, but he actually went off right at the opposite side towards the north west corner and then decided he would walk the length of the North stand around the Kop around the south to go back off, so got a lot of a lot of plaudits, I thought he did really really well, and potentially could have been man of the match, I was asked and I thought it was quite difficult really, because I thought Reece James did really well, I thought that Weaver did really well, I thought that when he got in amongst the ball killer done showed what he could be about, sort of with the way he picked it up and we sort of ran forward, I thought that Gray had a few good chances in the first half, where he actually picked the ball up, and he looked like a bit of an outlet coming forward when he did get the ball, yeah, I mean, Bannon I don’t know, they were responsible for their goal, somebody said, I think, I think you were, yeah, misplaced passes really, I think you know, midfield, that means tightening up, but it’s quite interesting because we’ve got to the end of the match and I just thought right, how do I feel about it, I actually felt like things that improved, like we’d taken a step forward, I think you know, conceding as we did, see the mistakes, and I thought to myself, if Dave Challenger, for instance, other managers are available, but Dave Challenger, if he was watching that, what would he be looking at and thinking, that’s something that needs to change, I haven’t really gone too much in depth, but it seems like he likes to press and have players that pull a finger out, and there are athletic, I thought, well, yeah, I mean, everybody did do the bit, but too many stray passes for my liking, as there has been for some time, but we showed a bit of willing and a bit of heart, certainly at times, it was back to when we we know we can, the way that we can play, yeah, so I felt not too bad about it really, and and you know, people around me saying, could have been worse, thought that was okay, so one one for manager last Wednesday, and I think that you know, it’s a good it’s a good place to build on if we hopefully we’re gonna get somebody in fairly quickly in it, and if it is Dave Challenger, then great, it could be quite a smooth transition, seems he knows some of the people around, just need Louis Barry back, he’s not necessarily answer, and you know, I think I think I’m feeling a bit more confident about about the Sunday match Blackpool, I think you know, we could we could actually get back on track it with a win, but yeah, we sort of took baby steps forward I think tonight, and people were relatively happy with what they saw, I think okay, so till till Friday when let’s see what’s see what the week brings, I’ll be talking about the the weekend and the fallout from Doncaster and better soon going and stuff like that, so I’ll talk about that on Friday till then, bye for now, and we’re all Wednesday aren’t we.

entry.title: 24/10/26 Doncaster 2-0 SWFC: Sideways and backwards
entry.content:
Introduction

Join us for a tough analysis of Sheffield Wednesday’s 2-0 loss to Doncaster Rovers. We’ll discuss the team’s poor performance, key player contributions, and the uncertain future under current management.

24/10/26 Doncaster 2-0 SWFC: Sideways and backwards

Five Minute View From The Kop

I don't quite know what happened there. Rather than put alongside Cooper, because Cooper was playing, rather than put a centre back alongside him, we decided to put Palmer in there.

Episode transcript

Chiffy Wednesday 5-minute view from The Kop after the new low of losing to Doncaster Rovers 2-0. I say new low because, thinking back to performances such as the Forest Green match, that time, it’s very difficult to actually know what I’ve actually seen there. So, we needed a reaction after Tuesday, yes, the Wimbledon match is still in our minds, but how can you be so good one minute and so poor the next? Tuesday was really, really poor, and then today, we knew we’d have to change things and it was a good opportunity to be able to stick players out there and give them an opportunity to do stuff.

When we lined up, I don’t know what happened with Gray. I expected Gray to be playing on the left, Morrison to be playing on the right, Keelah done in there, maybe Al Hamadi in there. Didn’t know what the situation had been regarding the centre backs, whether Cooper was going to be given a rest at any point, and who was going to be partnering him.

Managerial Uncertainty and Team Formation

Well, I can’t really quite work out because it seems that Morrison started at left wing back, people were saying that left wing back now he’s not a wing back and he doesn’t play generally on the left, so I don’t quite know what happened there. Rather than put alongside Cooper, because Cooper was playing, rather than put a centre back alongside him, we decided to put Palmer in there. When we got the opportunity, Weaver ended up being on the bench.

Mitchell and Bannon and Heskey playing, so I expected that Mitchell would be protecting that defence and that Bannon would be the creative one.

Billy Mitchell breaks the deadlock

I just, I’m not really sure that the team actually know what they’re doing at this moment in time.

And they played the first half when Doncaster scored both their goals, the team looked like they’d no idea what they were doing, they were absolutely all over the place, and Rovers took full advantage of that.

Key Player Contributions and Struggles

I’ll probably put Heskey as quite a played quite a big part in both those goals. He seemed like he just really was not picking up. I take it that he was the one that would be picking up Bailey, but he was there, but he just didn’t. So, you know, how were we going to change things and when we were going to change things? Well, decided that at half-time that Heskey was coming off and Birstow was coming on, so we’d be in a situation where we got two strikers on the pitch at the expense of a midfielder.

But yeah, Al Ahmadi did a lot of running around, missed some chances, Keyla Dunn behind him, who we’ve been calling for him to be playing, had a shocker of a match. He was he was definitely the worst worst player on the pitch today. He just scuffed everything, gave the ball away, he was just having an absolute nightmare.

I thought that we did actually improve second half, and we did actually push forward, but again, we push forward in the sense that against Knox County, I thought that one of the issues was that we, we were just as much as we took part in the match, competed, we just didn’t really create anything of any note. And I think whilst we did have we did have a few shots, this this match, I mean, actually, we had the majority of the ball possession, 66 percent, we had 13 shots, eight on target, they had 19 shots, six on target, and I think you know, you’re looking at sort of in the second half, 10, 10 shots, six on target, but a lot of those were just not that were like scuffed.

Bannon had a few, a couple of, couple of decent shots, Morrison once he got into it seemed to be seemed to be doing it, but yeah, just so many, so many issues at the moment, and I just don’t think the players really know what the plan is.

And Maynard Brewer, although he had his faults today, certainly with his kicking, he saved us really from it being probably about five-nil. A few good saves, Alfie May at one point actually we were pushing that forward up that far up that Alfie May managed to get through tackles going in, and I know the conditions were difficult, but they were difficult for both teams, um, and yeah, so Alfie May got through and uh, a one-on-one with the keeper, uh, may not bro managed to get a touch, uh, when he tried to get round, um, which actually delayed it, managed to get some defense back and we we we cleared it, but you know, we’re talking about defending against Doncaster Rovers who before the match were I think they were 18th, teams are down there for a reason, and we were top and now we’re slipping down, and you know, at what point, what what we’re looking for the changes, we’ve had a situation where other than uh Louis Barry, we’ve been able to keep quite a few players fit, uh, yes, I know that that we’ve had one or two players go out with injuries, but still, this team seems to be unable to, certainly, consistently play together, uh, and I just think that the way that that we we set up to play, um, we just seem to be a little bit all over the place, and and because of that, we try and pass the ball, we just seem to give it away so so often, we give it away so we can’t score, we can’t pass the ball properly, uh, and it seems that we’re now struggling to defend, um, and that’s not a team that’s going to be automatic, it’s not a team that’s going to be in the playoffs, and we may even struggle for mid-table.

So, where do we go from this point? It’s not about well, we need to wait until January and we’re going to get some players in, the players are there, I think we’ve got players there to to do well and you know be playoff contenders certainly, um, when everybody’s fit Wednesday playing at the best should be able to beat anybody in this league. When playing like they did certainly first half today, I can’t see us beating anybody, I think you know, when we go down to Bromley, I think we’re gonna we’re gonna struggle as things stand, I think we’re gonna struggle, so yeah, I mean, what is the what is there left to do?

There’s been a lot of calls for the manager to go, and you just, I mean, including today, lots and lots of uh shouts, um, the talks about you know, uh, sideways and backwards everywhere we go, but lots and lots of calls for uh Pederson to to go to leave, uh, and it’s it’s a shame because you know, I want it to work, I want him to get be given a good opportunity, but you’ve got to say if you’re going to be putting millions into into a club, and I know that he’d already said that it doesn’t matter if we don’t go up this season, but you want to see progress, and I think at the moment we’re just going backwards again, and some people have said that today seem very very much like last season, but we’ve got far better players, you know, so there’s no excuse really, so really you know now may be the time to question do we do we need to bring somebody in now, or if not, how long do we give it uh, and it’s just the the playing of the playing of people completely and utterly out of position when you’ve got opportunities to put people in that actually play in those positions, uh, with my very limited football management knowledge, I just don’t understand at all, so so let’s see how we go from this point on, let’s see what the fallout comes from from this match, I already know there’s going to be a complete meltdown for for them to get rid of the manager, um, there are people waiting there that are available, so let’s see uh, you know, upcoming we’ve got the um, we’ve got a couple of home games against Cambridge who are currently sixth, and then Blackpool are currently 20th, I’m not sure as things stand we’re going to be getting much change out of those out of those matches, so yeah, let’s see three days until we play Cambridge, let’s see what happens in that time okay, bye for now and we are still all Wednesday aren’t we.

entry.title: 20/10/26 Notts County 2-0 SWFC: A series of unfortunate events

link.title: 20/10/26 Notts County 2-0 SWFC: A series of unfortunate events

entry.content:
Introduction

Despite a 2-0 defeat, Sheffield Wednesday fans are divided in their reactions. In today’s Five Minute View from The Kop, we explore the setup, player performances, and future plans for the team as manager Pederson faces pressure to deliver results.

20/10/26 Notts County 2-0 SWFC: A series of unfortunate events

Five Minute View From The Kop

We're just not getting the balance right on the sides and in the middle as well.

Episode transcript

Billy Mitchell breaks the deadlock

Sheffield Wednesday five minute view from The Kop after the disappointing 2-0 defeat to Notch County a little bit later as I didn’t manage to get to see the match live last night as I was out but I’ve had a good look at it on the video today and I’ve also been looking around the socials. Obviously, everybody was absolutely in meltdown again, pedising out etc. , picking on various players and what have you. It’s actually quite good to be able to sit and watch it and to be able to scrub through and look at certain parts of the performance.

There were some people that were suggesting to me that it was an absolutely awful performance. Now what I’d say is that I don’t think so. I was looking for that. I was watching right from the start and looking for was the issue in the way that we were set up or was the issue specific players or was there some kind of turning point and I suppose the answer is that the answer is that there are a few things there.

Obviously, you know, the setup in the first place. I think the arguments after the occasion talking about Bernard can’t play two games in three days now. They can ban and now they can James. I think they can and I think we’ve got enough options to switch. We’re going to be enforced now to what we’re going to do for the next game against Doncaster at the weekend where we’ve got Jamal Low is going to be suspended. As far as I know, he’ll be suspended and so we’ll callum Slattery.

So are we going to bring Morrison on to the right? Are we going to give Kela Dunn his central forward role potentially with Alamiday or Bursto up there and let’s just see what’s happening with Bernard at the back if needs be. Is Otak Bao gonna be dropping in or are we gonna if we’ve not already sent him away are we gonna bring Ernie Weaver in? Which again, you know, it may be a better option even just for the moment.

Whilst I’ll take by I was getting so much stick because he certainly does seem to be the full guy as well as Pederson. So there’s a few things there obviously.

Bernard’s substitution and penalty

You know, the Bernard going off the replacing him with Otak Bao and giving away the penalty and then Low getting sent off taking taking Bannon off. You know, I think we’ve then our creativity has been taken out of the off the pitch at that point. So we’re not really going to do that much. Looking at the momentum of the game, it was mostly them pretty spiky. It was like you know uh wanting going forward and creating a chance rather than it being sort of like playing in the middle of the park.

So there’s a lot of potential options on there. So yeah, disappointing really. And I think you know everybody’s got a certain amount of blame to take on it. I spoke a little bit more in depth today because I think that there’s more to work to that that performance and meets the eye. I think you know there’s there’s a few things. Pederson says that we need to learn quickly. I think you know he needs to learn quickly as well.

And try and sort out what’s actually happening with the team. We’ve got the players at the moment. We’re just not getting the balance right on the sides and in the middle as well. We’ve been saved previously by the good defense. But are we putting too much emphasis on the defense and are we actually making really really hard work of this? I’m not saying that we should be pissing the league and it should be dead easy. But I just think that again some some sides.

And last night you know you you would like to hope that a manager is going to say right I want you to hit him I want you to hit him hard right from the off. We’re going to um we’re going to just go at them rather than this idea of transitions which seems to be a favorite thing of Pederson to talk about. Rather than this uh you know we’ll we’ll hit him on the break. Well we didn’t we didn’t hit him on the break.

You know we were every time we knocked the ball forward it seemed to be just coming straight back at us. So you know we weren’t finding the patters. We’ve got nobody running on the right hand side. I thought you know Gray tried his best on the left. We’re not a one-man team. Louie Barry’s going to be uh hopefully amazing when he comes back but you know we we need to not just rely upon him. Gray’s a good player so he’s Morrison.

Let’s just find that balance right. As for Pederson now, yeah, he’s not doing himself any favors at all really.

The need for Plan B

We’re not really seen plan B. We’re not really seeing a good plan A. Really just to start off with. We’ll just have to see what happens against Doncaster. If we have another poor performance if we don’t manage to get anything out of that game then yeah you know I think it’s the writing’s on the wall really.

Okay, that’s it for me for now and until uh the Friday briefing right until later. We’re all Wednesday aren’t we?

entry.title: 17/10/26 SWFC 5-0 Wimbledon: Hawaii five-o owls
entry.content:
Introduction

Sheffield Wednesday delivered a resounding 5-0 victory against Wimbledon, a performance that had many questioning the team’s form. Managerial decisions and the versatile play of players were key factors in the win. Tune in for a detailed breakdown of the game and insights from The Kop.

17/10/26 SWFC 5-0 Wimbledon: Hawaii five-o owls

Five Minute View From The Kop

But you know, we're one of the biggest scorers in the league, we're one of the tightest defenses in the league. It's not really a bad situation really is it?

Episode transcript

Chefy Wednesday five minute view from The Kop. Well, what a day, Hawaii 5-0 5-0 against Wimbledon. Well, in the preview, I was previously saying that this was a team that didn’t score any goals. This was a team that had got injuries at the back. They look certainly very shaky at the back. And we were just looking for Wednesday to put that aside. They would actually take advantage of that somehow, try and fit such as Keyla Dunne in Al Amadee in there.

And it was interesting actually what I didn’t expect was for Slattery to be moved out onto the right so to speak and Keyla Dunne to be brought into the middle. But certainly worked. Keyla Dunne had a fantastic game, but then again, everybody on the pitch had a great game. I think every single one of them. You can look at it. I think probably the one on the pitch that really had a little bit less to do was Jamal Lowe in that sense.

So we scored five goals, but actually, the person that we stuck up front was what wasn’t one of them. I have some fantastic goals today and just everybody just seemed to be pulling the weight. Obviously, I think you can just put Slattery anywhere. I think you know, if he’s gonna be busy, wherever so to stick him on the right, Morrison was on the bench on the left. We got Gray. We got Keyla Dunne from. We’d got Maynard Brewer in in the net, which I sort of didn’t expect, but again, I have no issues with any of the goalkeepers.

I think they’ve all shown that the they can all play the part. And you know, we’ve got this five games in 15 days. I think they were saying so we’ve got to make sure that we are rotating this this squad. And you know, the other thing as well is that Jay Neske was given a shot in midfield. I think he’s deserved it and I think you know, again, he played very well today. Not really at the expense of Billy Mitchell.

See, Billy Mitchell. He was on the bench and I think when you think about players that are gonna be so busy, certainly integral parts of Wednesday, the fact that we could bring Billy Mitchell off and and he came on and did his thing and was fantastic. You know, Morrison came on and interestingly when Morrison came on, he came on for Gray, who’s who had a great game on the on the left? And Morrison went on the left and seemed to be getting a bit more of the ball.

Whereas on the right-hand side, you didn’t you know, and again, the fantastic support that you get from from Reese James. He’s been a great player this season and why we, um, Denard over bringing him in. I don’t know. I don’t know what the situation with that was or what happened at Rotherham, but you know, he’s been fantastic this season and he’s great support for whoever’s in front of him. So when it’s been Louis Barry, when it’s been Harry Gray, he’s he’s been there for support for overlap, really really good.

Bannon chipped in with a goal today again, fantastic. In fact, they only had one. Seemed that they only had one goal image that they put up on the on the scoreboard and that was of Barry Bannon. So Bannon scored, he put that up, Gray scored, they put Bannon up, etc. Gray scored a absolute rocket of a shot, but you know, all the goals were good, even if they ended up being tappings, they were just worked so well.

And there were people saying that this is the poorest opposition I’ve seen this season. Barbara O’Mley. Well, yeah, I sort of get what you’re saying, but you know, we were playing a team that were 12th in the league that had, you know, got a not a bad record. People were saying that we were only any good because we’d all we’d only played poor teams and when we’d played the higher teams, we’d not done so well against them.

Yeah, fair enough. I get that. You know, we lost to Bradford who I think went top of the league and they’ve only scored ten goals. But you know, we’re one of the biggest scorers in the in the league, we’re one of the tightest defenses in the league. It’s not really a bad situation really is it? And and fantastic at the end to a away 5-0. Played which they must have been waiting for that one. I did say to somebody I really like this league on days like this to actually play and come comfortably beat a team, you know, they didn’t really give us any major problems at all.

And you’ve got to not just say the opposition were poor. I think that we did exactly the right thing now. Could you stick that down to the manager? Well, I want to sticks like I want to suck Slattery out on the right. Certainly wouldn’t. I would have probably looked at you know, if you’re gonna drop Billy Mitchell or Barry Bannon are being slightly into midfield, keep with Morrison on the right ground a left, but you know, I’m not a football manager.

And I’m sure that they’ve tried these things and see what works so that is an option because Keyla Dunn is a very very busy player. So he’s Barry Bannon. So he’s Billy Mitchell. So he’s Calum’s lottery.

Versatile Play and Managerial Decisions

And I think having all these options on the pitch just gives us so much. You know, the interchanging of the passes between them was really really good today as well. And it looked like Alamedy when he came on was just so pissed off that he didn’t really get the opportunity to be able to score against his former team because everybody was wanting to have a go. So Morrison came on and he was shooting from all over the place.

Slattery was shooting from all over place. Keyla done. He scored two. He wanted to get his hat trick. So what a what an absolutely fantastic day and you know, give the given a manager some some slack and give the players some slack and just so okay on to the next one on Tuesday and let’s see let’s see where we go on from there and see whether we can push on from now on. There will be people out there just saying well it will Wimbledon they were rubbish.

No, this is a mid-table team and we dispatched them and played really really really well. That doesn’t make seeming to say that we’re gonna storm the league now. There’s only a couple points in it. But surprisingly, we were sixth, we were fourth at one point, but it seems that these teams around is winning. But we’ve got games in hand and I think if we win our games in and we’re going to, you know, we’re gonna be up there.

As we should with the squad that we’ve got with the support that we’ve got, you know, we should be up where we are. We should be minimum playoffs, so fantastic day anyway, and let’s see what Tuesday brings until then. We’re all Wednesday, aren’t we?

entry.content:
Introduction

Welcome to the Five Minute View From The Kop, where we dissect the recent Sheffield Wednesday match against Huddersfield. Two goals, two draws, and a rollercoaster of emotions. Who will be the star of the show, and what does this result mean for the team moving forward?

10/10/26 Huddersfield 2-2 SWFC: Owls get out of jail

Five Minute View From The Kop

They had all the best chances, and we didn't have a single shot on goal. Very, very frustrating.

Episode transcript

Sheffield Wednesday, five minute view from The Kop, well what a game, what a strange game. Huddersfield 2, Sheffield Wednesday 2. Wednesday putting out a strong team. I did wonder whether Davis-Keillor-Dunn would be starting up front, but they put Jamal Lowe up front and DeShawn Bernard came back into defence with Santos out. Other than that, the team were pretty much as it was with Harry Gray and Morrison on the wings. Now they came at us, put us under pressure when we had the ball, when they had the ball, they were passing it very well.

We saw a lot of the ball in the first half, they had all the best chances, and we didn’t have a single shot on goal. Very, very frustrating to have such a decent team out just playing as ever with the same formation with a 4-2-3-1, one up front. Ball just coming back, Jamal Lowe, nothing really coming out of that. Midfield, lots and lots of battling you could say, but we weren’t really getting anywhere. We were trying to go up the wings, but really this gelling that we were sort of expecting to happen has just not really been happening.

The passers were going astray, there seemed to be a lot of passers going astray, and as I say, we were about 60-40 in possession to us, so we’ve seen a lot of the ball, but we were giving the ball away quite a lot. They had a number of opportunities, Joan Lumley a couple that I remember where he one-handed saves really, really, really well done and he seemed to be the star player. You just thought, well, if anybody’s going to score, it’s going to be Huddersfield and we’re just going to try and hang on and hopefully just get a point out of it, something like that.

The second half started and straight away they scored. And again, we gave the ball away. I think it was Lumley went to kick it out, kicked it out short, Reece James had to race to get it, managed to get a foot on it, but then it went to the player, and Joe Taylor he scored with that first one. And then so that was just after kick-off, and then 60-70 minutes in, again, the ball just seemed to come, it was quite a long, long ball that was sent, passed straight across, lots and lots of defenders just stood around staring.

We’d got plenty back, but they just passed it through us, and it was a really easy goal. At that point, you know, you just thought, even though we’ve got the possession, Huddersfield were the team that wanted to win that match. We didn’t look like we were getting anywhere, and I think it was quite late on when we actually had the first shot of any sort. Never mind, a shot on target, just like a shot at that stage, but you’ve got to say all credit to Wednesday, we made some subs.

Again, well, Keelah Dunn came on, and you thought, oh, where’s he going to be. And then I don’t know whether we were playing like supposedly like a two up front with Jamal Lowe, but Keelah Dunn was certainly playing further forward that first half, we were so narrow. I say narrow as in flat, narrow. This is almost as if we were playing a 5-5-0 with like nobody up front, but yeah, Keelah Dunn played a little bit further forward, and I mean 88 minutes, you just thought, well, we ain’t gonna get anything out of this at all, 88 minutes.

Ball comes over, and player got an header on it, went straight into the net, but it was their player, really, surprised it was just really out of nothing, not under masses of pressure. 2-1, you just thought, well, okay, fair enough. Really at that point, they seemed to be on the back foot. However, I think it was a combination of they thought two-nil, that’s it, the game’s over, we’ve done our job now. I mean, they were even sticking even stuck on Ashley Fletcher, probably thinking, you know, well, this is this is it, you know, we’re gonna we just turn the screw, but as I say, 88 minutes, and we just kept going.

Then I was actually listening to their commentary, and so one-sided it really is, one-sided. Um, then the ball we were flinging the ball into the box quite a lot, ball came over, and their player really, I thought, kicked, um, kicked Liam Cooper straight in the face to the extent that he got blood pouring down his face, he had to go off immediately, uh, and they brought Palmer on, um, but yeah, they, they’re on their commentary and radio leads were saying, well, I’m not sure really whether it was uh, was a penalty or not, Cooper’s got blood pouring down his face, and you could see that he’d been kicked in the face, and it weren’t one of those where he stooped, he actually, he didn’t stoop at all, but still got kicked in the face, absolute stonewall penalty, I know I’m biased, but uh, and obviously Jamal Lowe is where he’s really handy to have him on the pitch.

I mean, you know, you could have said really, I didn’t know whether it’d be worth starting him, but the fact that Jamal Lowe were on the pitch, yes, he took the penalty, seems to be, um, best penalty taker, and he really got involved. I thought before that, Mitchell put a lot of, a lot of effort in, seemed to be, uh, more coming from Mitchell than than Bannon and Slattery can all three play together, I’m not sure we we’ve got a look really what we want to do is the potential to take one of those out of the equation, switch it, leave the other one on the bench to switch it for the latter part of the game, maybe even that’s if that’s uh, Barry Bannon potentially, but you know, he does dictate a match, uh, and then maybe give us a couple up front, um, Birstow came on towards the end, and uh, and again, you know, was playing very far forward, so we were really giving him a much much tougher game towards the end, but why can’t we have done that in the first place, we were way off it, that first half, absolutely way off it, and who do you blame, do you blame the players, you blame the manager, is it the way we set up, I don’t really agree with the way that we set up, uh, but at the same time, they’ve got to they’ve got to take some responsibility.

And I know a lot of people say, well, just change the manager, and it’ll magically all come together, I don’t, you just don’t know, you’ve got to have given him the opportunity. I think a point today is good, I think some of the other points that we’ve got have not really been good enough if we’re looking at we were looking at automatic weren’t we at one point, I think we’re now, um, I think we’re now seventh in the table, um, although we’ve got a couple of couple of matches in some cases to play, uh, on such as Plymouth who were up at the top, they played two games more, um, but yeah, it’s frustrating, so frustrating, me in a Wednesday fan, first half awful, second half yeah, I mean, the radio were obviously saying others fields didn’t get what they deserved, I think on balance, two two, it’s pretty, uh, pretty fair result, although I would say we really got out of jail last couple of minutes, well, it’s our last couple of minutes because we scored in 88, and then it was actually 98 by the time the penalty got taken, um, definite penalty, their own goal was terrible really for them from their point of view, the two goals that we conceived in the first half were defensive mistakes, you’ve got to say, and I thought we cut that out on a positive note to finish off, um, DeShawn Bernard came in and played quite a chunk of the match, he played 69 minutes, and I will say that he actually, um, he actually played well, uh, I thought it would probably gonna be too much too soon for him, but actually, I thought he looked he looked very steady, so that’s good, um, I would expect more from Morrison to be fair, uh, I thought Gray did okay, but I think on the other side, Morrison didn’t really, he’s not really got that thing going on with Valerate that having Reece James who you’re getting a little bit stick today, but he just, he gets involved, he gets involved in everything, he wants to get involved playing stuff forward, so I think between him and Gray, I thought down the left, we looked we looked good, so absolute relief, uh, and uh, yeah, plenty of nerves today, uh, two two is is okay, and we sort of push on to uh, to the next game, it’s good that football’s back in again, uh, after the international break, who’ve we got next, we’ve got Wimbledon, uh, next week at Hillsborough, and Wimbledon currently at mid-table, this needs to be a nice comfortable victory if it’s not, if it’s a draw, if it’s a loss, we really need to do something, okay, well, that’s it for me for now, see you later, we’re all Wednesday aren’t we.
